core.title: Graph resolver: resolve or report, never fabricate a node
core.given: The resolver that turns relationship attributes on authored documents into graph edges.
core.when: You plan, specify or change how that resolver builds the graph.
core.then: The resolver MUST build the declared-id set first, admit an edge only if its target is in that set, and report every other edge as a finding. It must never synthesize a node for an undeclared target and never silently drop the edge.
prefer: Write the acceptance so that it asserts the graph NODE COUNT directly, not merely the finding. An unresolved edge adds no node.
Also assert that every unresolved edge appears as a reported finding, so that none is silently dropped.
avoid: An ensure-node-on-edge pattern: the edge-insertion path creates a bare node for any target it has not seen and applies it to BOTH endpoints of every edge. Any edge that names a non-existent target conjures that target into being.
unless: Nothing is exempt from the no-fabrication half. There is no configuration that permits synthesis.
An absent attribute is not an unresolved edge. Only declared relationships are resolved.
core.why: Fabrication is worse than absence. An absent parent leaves an orphan, and an orphan check catches it. A fabricated parent makes the node look CONNECTED, which defeats that check.
evidence: A resolver test asserts the graph node count directly. Adding an edge to an undeclared target leaves the node count unchanged.
The same test asserts that each unresolved edge appears as a REPORTED finding, so that none is dropped.
verification: Strict disposition, severity 1: every finding fails the check; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline. Nothing is exempt from the no-fabrication half — no configuration permits synthesis.

A validator rebuilds the declared-id set from the authored corpus before resolving any edge, and reports every edge whose target is outside it. Resolve or report, never invent: a target outside the set is a REPORTED finding, is never synthesized into a node, and is never silently dropped. Fabrication — creating a graph node for a target no document declares, so that an edge appears to resolve — is the defect the check exists to make impossible.

The discipline is asserted on the graph NODE COUNT, not merely on the finding: fabrication defeats an orphan check more thoroughly than absence does, because a fabricated parent makes the node look connected.
The check does not cover absent relationship attributes: only declared relationships are resolved, so an absent attribute is not an unresolved edge.
The check relies on the declared-id set being closed and enumerable; that is what lets this derived graph hold resolve-or-report where an open-ended identifier space cannot.

fires: A planner writes the plan artifact or acceptance for the graph resolver.
A change to how the resolver handles an edge whose target is not declared.
A proposal to make unresolved targets a warning, to drop them quietly, or to add a stub node for them.
doesNotFire: Pure authored-document writing with no resolver work. The author-side rule of this convention covers that, and it requires this part.

profileRequirements.meaning: The authored-document kind whose relationship attributes the resolver reads; the corpus from which the declared-id set is built.
The stack's plan-artifact kind that a planner writes when specifying the resolver, referenced by the activation's planner scenario.
How an authored document declares its graph identifier; the declared-id set is built from these declarations before any edge is resolved.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself (declared-id set first, resolve or report, never fabricate, never silently drop) was already stack-neutral and is kept verbatim. Non-neutral residue: (1) the sibling author-side rule is referenced generically ('the author-side rule of this convention'); its concrete id (.author-declared-target) stays in bun.json; (2) the comparison with this stack's traceability graph and the reproduced incident (147/168 edges, #1758) are bunOnly motivation, not obligation; (3) the authored-corpus id-declaration syntax had no closed-vocabulary key, so idiom.docs_syntax#doc_id_declaration is proposed; (4) the change-observer value ids (docs_resolver_*_changed) are realization wiring kept bunOnly, with the fact itself neutral and still needs_new_observer; (5) the resolver component's location is not profiled because bun.json never states one — only the change-observer note does, which is bunOnly.
